featured.title: A Judge Killed the $100,000 H-1B Fee. Why Indians Shouldn't Celebrate Just Yet
featured.excerpt: A Boston court struck down Trump's surcharge nationwide on June 8 — but a conflicting D.C. ruling means the real fight is now headed for the Supreme Court, and nobody's getting refunds.
featured.image_caption: The U.S. Supreme Court building in Washington; conflicting rulings have thrown the $100,000 H-1B fee into legal limbo (Wikimedia Commons)
featured.nri_angle: Indians make up over 70% of approved H-1B petitions, so no group has more riding on whether the $100,000 surcharge survives appeal — and the current relief is provisional, not permanent.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Heading for Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years. The Bill Will Land on Dinner Tables — Including the Diaspora's.
news.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has left the 2026 monsoon delayed and deficient, with the IMD forecasting the lowest rainfall since 2015, Mumbai rationing water, and coffee, sugar and pulse crops already at risk.
news.image_caption: Monsoon rains over an Indian field; the 2026 season is the country's weakest in 11 years
news.nri_angle: A failing monsoon stokes food inflation and pushes New Delhi toward rice and sugar export curbs — the moves that spike basmati and onion prices in diaspora grocery stores abroad — while pressuring the rupee and the returns NRIs earn on Indian deposits, and threatening the incomes of relatives still farming back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The $100,000 H-1B Fee Is Back. Indian Tech Workers Who Celebrated Its Defeat Have 72 Hours of Whiplash to Show for It.
news.excerpt: A Boston judge struck down the fee on June 8, then paused his own order on June 12 — so as of June 17 the $100,000 charge is again in force, with conflicting rulings in three courts pointing toward the Supreme Court.
news.image_caption: The Boston skyline; a federal judge in Boston struck down the H-1B fee on June 8, then paused his own order four days later
news.nri_angle: Nearly three-quarters of H-1B visas go to Indians, so a reinstated $100,000 fee threatens the principal on-ramp for Indian engineers, doctors and researchers — and the on-again, off-again legal whiplash forces diaspora families, students and physicians to make irreversible decisions against a rule that can flip in 72 hours.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The India-US Trade Deal Is Entering the Home Stretch. America's Top Trade Negotiator Lands in Delhi Monday.
news.excerpt: USTR Jamieson Greer visits India on June 23-24 to finalise the framework agreement, with Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal predicting the first tranche could be executed by mid-July.
news.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who says the first tranche of the India-US trade deal could be done by mid-July
news.nri_angle: A trade deal reshapes the fortunes of the Indian exporters, IT-services firms and pharma companies that employ diaspora professionals, and directly shifts costs for Indian-American importers of textiles, jewellery and generic drugs — while knitting the two countries the diaspora bridges ever closer.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Indian IT Stocks Just Crashed to a Three-Year Low. One Warning From Accenture Did It.
news.excerpt: The Nifty IT index sank as much as 5.6 percent on June 19, with TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCLTech falling 5-8 percent, after Accenture flagged cautious client spending and an AI-driven shift that threatens the sector's labour-heavy model.
news.image_caption: The Infosys campus in Bengaluru; the Nifty IT index sank to a three-year low on June 19
news.nri_angle: India's IT majors are the largest sponsors of H-1B visas and the biggest employers of diaspora technologists abroad, so a demand slowdown colliding with a tighter US visa regime and AI layoffs threatens the very job pipeline that carried many NRIs overseas — even as the sector's heavy weighting in the Nifty hits diaspora portfolios directly.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Reliance Just Filed for the Jio IPO. It Could Be the Biggest Stock Debut in India's History.
news.excerpt: At the Reliance AGM on June 19, Mukesh Ambani said Jio Platforms' draft prospectus was filed with SEBI — a fresh issue of up to 27 crore shares targeting roughly $4 billion, on a business brokerages value near $180 billion.
news.image_caption: Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani, who announced the Jio Platforms IPO filing at the AGM
news.nri_angle: The Jio IPO offers NRIs a rare large-cap, liquid way to own the infrastructure behind 500 million Indian internet users — investable through NRE/NRO portfolio accounts — and stands as a real-time referendum on whether the diaspora and the world still believe in India's digital growth story.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Banks Want to Lend Dollars Out of GIFT City. The Target: $55 Billion in Diaspora Money.
news.excerpt: Lenders are asking the RBI to route loans through their offshore GIFT City units to amplify a revived FCNR deposit scheme — a 2013-style bid to pull in diaspora dollars and steady a rupee just recovering toward 94.
news.image_caption: The GIFT One tower at Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, India offshore financial hub
news.nri_angle: New Delhi is openly competing for NRI savings: rising FCNR deposit rates, hedging subsidies and a proposed GIFT City lending mechanism could channel up to $55 billion in diaspora dollars into India, handing overseas Indians an outsized role in defending the rupee and earning more attractive, currency-risk-free returns.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Quietly Rewrote Its Foreigner Registration Rules. NRI Families With Foreign-Passport Kids Need to Read the Fine Print.
news.excerpt: The Immigration and Foreigners (Amendment) Rules, 2026 — in force since June 1 — scrap the old 14-day grace period for long-stay registration, allow late filing only in 'emergent circumstances,' and impose a new 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later takes a foreign citizenship.
news.image_caption: A Republic of India Emergency Certificate, an official government travel document; new 2026 rules tighten registration duties for foreign nationals in India
news.nri_angle: India's new 2026 immigration rules scrap the 14-day registration grace period for long-staying foreigners and impose a 30-day reporting duty on parents whose India-born child later acquires foreign citizenship — changes that directly affect OCI holders, NRIs with foreign-national spouses, and diaspora families raising children across two passports.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India and Canada Want a Trade Deal Signed This Year. For Three Million Indians in Canada, the Reset Is Personal.
news.excerpt: Meeting on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian — their fourth in under a year — Narendra Modi and Mark Carney pledged to conclude a long-stalled Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement by the G20, aiming to double bilateral trade to $50 billion and explicitly leaning on the diaspora as the bridge between the two countries.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Canadian PM Mark Carney; the two leaders met on the sidelines of the G7 in Evian
news.nri_angle: India and Canada set a G20 deadline to conclude a long-stalled trade deal and double bilateral trade to $50 billion — a reset that directly affects the roughly three million people of Indian origin in Canada through talent-mobility, student-exchange and services provisions, after a two-year freeze that hit the diaspora's people-to-people ties hardest.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The RBI Just Told Banks to Pay NRIs Whatever It Takes. Deposit Rates Have Already Jumped to 7%.
news.excerpt: In a move last used during the 2013 Taper Tantrum, the Reserve Bank has scrapped interest-rate ceilings on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits until September 30 and is absorbing banks' hedging costs — a direct bid for the diaspora's dollars that has pushed rates from around 3% to as high as 7.1%.
news.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai; the central bank scrapped rate caps on NRI deposits on June 17
news.nri_angle: The RBI has temporarily lifted rate caps on FCNR(B) and long-term NRE deposits, pushing returns from ~3% to as high as 7.1% — a rare, time-limited chance for NRIs to earn high, low-risk returns on dollars or rupees parked in Indian banks, but only until September 30 and with tricky rules on breaking older deposits.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Court Just Lifted a $100,000 Wall in Front of Immigrant Doctors. Indian-American Physicians Are Calling It a Win for Patients.
news.excerpt: The American Association of Physicians of Indian Origin has welcomed a federal ruling striking down the Trump administration's $100,000 H-1B fee, warning the charge would have gutted rural and safety-net hospitals where international medical graduates — a large share of them Indian-trained — keep the lights on.
news.image_caption: A United States federal courthouse; a federal judge struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee this week
news.nri_angle: A federal court struck down the $100,000 H-1B fee that Indian-American physician group AAPI says would have crippled rural and safety-net hospitals — where Indian-trained doctors (21% of US immigrant physicians) are essential — but with an appeal likely and other anti-H-1B bills moving, the relief for the diaspora's medical community may be temporary.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Oil Lifeline Through Hormuz Is Reopening. The Peace Holding It Open Just Wobbled.
news.excerpt: Tankers are moving through the Strait of Hormuz again after the US-Iran ceasefire, and an Indian-flagged ship is finally sailing home. But Friday's signing ceremony in Switzerland was scrapped, Iran is threatening transit fees, and roughly half of India's crude still rides on a 60-day truce.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; tankers resumed transiting the Strait of Hormuz this week after the US-Iran ceasefire
news.nri_angle: Roughly half of India's crude and a huge share of its trade ride through the Strait of Hormuz, where nearly half its overseas migrants and seafarers work — so the strait reopening means steadier Gulf jobs, cheaper goods and a calmer rupee, while the 60-day truce's fragility keeps diaspora-held energy and shipping stocks on edge.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Is Handing Its UAE Passport and Visa Counters to a New Operator on July 1. Millions of NRIs Need to Pay Attention.
news.excerpt: From July 1, Al Hind Tours and Travels takes over passport, visa, OCI and attestation services across the Emirates — replacing BLS International and SGIVS Global. For the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE, every consular errand is about to run through a different door.
news.image_caption: An Indian passport; renewals, OCI cards and attestations in the UAE move to a new service provider on July 1
news.nri_angle: Every passport renewal, OCI application and attestation for the 3.5 million Indians in the UAE — the world's largest expatriate Indian community — moves to a new operator on July 1, so families should finish what they can before June 30 and trust only official Embassy channels for what comes next.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Fuel Retailers Have Hit Their Borrowing Limit Absorbing Rs 1 Trillion in Losses to Keep Pump Prices Frozen
news.excerpt: Oil secretary Neeraj Mittal says state-run IOC, BPCL and HPCL can barely borrow more after eating Rs 1 lakh crore of first-quarter losses to shield Indian consumers from the Iran war's oil shock. The freeze cannot hold forever — and the diaspora's families pay either way.
news.image_caption: An Indian Oil fuel station; state retailers have absorbed about Rs 1 trillion in losses to keep pump prices frozen
news.nri_angle: India has frozen pump prices through the oil shock by making state retailers borrow against Rs 1 trillion in losses — a cushion that keeps inflation and the relatives NRIs support protected for now, but whose eventual breaking point will hit household budgets, the rupee and diaspora-held energy stocks alike.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Modi Hands Out Rs 2,400 Crore to First-Time Workers Today. It's a Bet That India's Jobs Problem Can Be Bought Down.
news.excerpt: At Vigyan Bhawan on Friday, the Prime Minister disburses the first big tranche of the Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana — a Rs 99,446 crore scheme that pays young Indians to enter the formal economy and pays employers to hire them.
news.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who disbursed Rs 2,400 crore under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana on June 19
news.nri_angle: India is spending Rs 99,446 crore to pull its young workforce into the formal economy — a bet that, if it works, means households less dependent on diaspora remittances and a stronger demographic case for every NRI weighing an investment back home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: After Years of Delay, India's Biggest Stock Exchange Files to Go Public. The NSE IPO Could Be Worth $57 Billion.
news.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives market — has finally filed draft IPO papers, setting up a $2.6 billion windfall for its investors and a landmark listing that lands just as India throws its equity markets open to NRIs.
news.image_caption: The National Stock Exchange of India, which filed draft papers for a landmark IPO
news.nri_angle: India is listing the exchange at the heart of its markets just as it raises the limits on how much NRIs can own in Indian companies — a one-two move that courts the diaspora as a permanent class of domestic-market investors.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Rewrote the Rulebook for 4.5 Million OCI Holders. The Fine Print Forces a Hard Choice on Dual-Passport Families.
news.excerpt: A sweeping overhaul moves Overseas Citizen of India casework fully online and promises 15-day approvals, but a mandatory passport-update rule with fines, colliding with new US disclosure demands, leaves diaspora families caught between two governments.
news.image_caption: An Indian passport and travel documents; India has overhauled the OCI program for its global diaspora
news.nri_angle: OCI holders ARE the diaspora — 4.5 million of them — and this overhaul both speeds up their casework and, colliding with new US disclosure rules, forces dual-passport families into a long-deferred choice between an American and an Indian passport.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Mumbai Has 40 Days of Drinking Water Left, and the Monsoon Is Running on Empty
news.excerpt: The city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs sink to roughly 10 per cent of capacity, forcing water cuts on construction and industry while Maharashtra waits on a monsoon that may be the weakest in 11 years.
news.image_caption: The Mumbai skyline; the city is enduring its driest June in over a decade as reservoirs run low
news.nri_angle: The huge Mumbai and Maharashtra diaspora has family weathering the cuts firsthand, while a weak monsoon stokes food inflation that quietly raises the real cost of the money NRIs send home.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Arms Factories Just Hit a Record, and the Private Sector Is Finally Getting a Real Cut
news.excerpt: Defence production touched an all-time high of ₹1.78 lakh crore in FY26 as exports surged past ₹38,000 crore — the clearest sign yet that India's bid to turn from the world's biggest arms importer into a maker and seller is gaining traction.
news.image_caption: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, who announced India's record defence production for FY26
news.nri_angle: A diaspora that has long watched India rank as the world's biggest arms importer now sees it building and exporting its own security, with the defence-tech boom drawing in exactly the high-skilled, globally networked talent the diaspora is full of.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Just Made Its NRI Savings Accounts the Best Deal in Years. The Window Closes September 30.
nri-world.excerpt: The RBI scrapped interest-rate caps on NRE and FCNR(B) deposits, and banks are already offering 7%. The fine print is where the diaspora should look twice.
nri-world.image_caption: Hands holding ₹500 notes; the RBI's deposit-rate relaxation is aimed at pulling NRI dollars into Indian banks.
nri-world.nri_angle: For overseas Indians, parking money back home has always been about more than yield. A temporary RBI relaxation now pairs that sentiment with the most competitive deposit rates in years—and a short clock.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Oldest Indian Association Swore In a New President. The Congratulatory Letters Told the Real Story.
nri-world.excerpt: When a community-group inauguration draws written tribute from a US senator and a state attorney general, the diaspora has stopped seeking recognition and started expecting it.
nri-world.image_caption: Members of the Indian-American community in traditional attire at a festive gathering.
nri-world.nri_angle: The small ceremonies of community organisations are where a scattered immigrant population connects to the levers of American civic life. The AIA's swearing-in is a quiet index of how far Indian-Americans have travelled.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: France Is Getting Its First Traditional Hindu Temple, Carved in India and Rebuilt Stone by Stone Near Paris
nri-world.excerpt: A community builds in permanent stone when it has decided it is staying. In a country defined by laïcité, that is a particularly pointed statement.
nri-world.image_caption: A BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, built in the traditional carved-stone style France's new temple will share.
nri-world.nri_angle: A temple carved in India and reassembled in Europe is a literal rendering of what the diaspora does with its heritage—carrying the original across an ocean and rebuilding it as an anchor for the next generation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Wants to Build India's Story a Permanent Home in Washington. It Will Cost $14 Million.
nri-world.excerpt: After eight years of quiet research, the team behind the India Heritage Center is launching an aggressive campaign for a 20,000-square-foot museum in the US capital — ten galleries tracing 11,000 years of civilisation, aimed as much at mainstream America as at the next generation of Indian-Americans.
nri-world.image_caption: A museum in Washington, DC; the proposed India Heritage Center would join the capital's cultural institutions
nri-world.nri_angle: A proposed $14 million India Heritage Center in Washington would give the Indian-American story its first permanent civilisational museum in the US — a test of whether a community that has succeeded materially will fund its own cultural memory for the next generation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Connecticut Diaspora Chapter Turned 20. Its Guest List Was a Map of How Far Indian-Americans Have Come.
nri-world.excerpt: GOPIO-CT honored a state senator, a bank CEO, and three others at its 20th anniversary gala — and gave away $50,000 to two non-Indian local charities in the process.
nri-world.image_caption: Hands raise a trophy skyward, evoking the awards presented at a community recognition gala
nri-world.nri_angle: For Indian-Americans, founding a cultural association is easy; keeping one alive for two decades is the hard part. GOPIO-CT's milestone shows what it takes for an immigrant community organization to outlive its founders and graduate from Diwali dinners to public policy, youth charity, and a recognized voice in state affairs.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: America's Oldest Indian Association Honored Seven 'Jewels.' The List Doubled as a Census of the Diaspora.
nri-world.excerpt: Founded in 1967, AIA-NY has watched the entire arc of Indian migration to America. Its 2026 gala honored oncologists, a transplant pioneer, and a Harvard MBA building an AI startup.
nri-world.nri_angle: An honoree list is a quiet census. AIA-NY's seven 'Ratnas' track exactly where Indian-Americans have concentrated — heavy in medicine, rising in tech and finance — while documenting a generational handoff from five-decade veterans to a 20-something founder. It also shows the value of an institution that has outlasted six decades of arrivals.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora's Most Remarkable 2025 Election Win Came From an Island of 1.4 Million — and a Great-Granddaughter of Indentured Laborers
nri-world.excerpt: Kamla Persad-Bissessar, sworn in for a second term as Trinidad and Tobago's prime minister, complicates the Silicon-Valley story of Indian success abroad with a far older one.
nri-world.image_caption: Kamla Persad-Bissessar, prime minister of Trinidad and Tobago and a descendant of Indian indentured laborers
nri-world.nri_angle: The dominant narrative of the Indian diaspora fixates on recent, professional, US-and-UK arrivals. Trinidad's 180-year-old Indian community — descendants of indentured estate laborers — is the diaspora's longest experiment in what Indian identity becomes after a century and a half away from India. Persad-Bissessar's return puts that story back at the center.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: She Was in Third Place on Election Night. A Week of Counting Made Her a Contender to Run Los Angeles.
nri-world.excerpt: Coimbatore-born councilmember Nithya Raman overtook a reality-TV upstart to reach the November runoff against Mayor Karen Bass — a race that could put a daughter of the diaspora atop America's second-largest city.
nri-world.image_caption: Los Angeles City Councilmember Nithya Raman, who advanced to the November mayoral runoff against incumbent Karen Bass
nri-world.nri_angle: More than a million South Asians live in California, the largest such population in the U.S. A Raman victory in November would place an Indian-born immigrant at the head of Los Angeles, its $15B budget and the 2028 Olympics — a marker of how far Indian-American political power has moved from the margins to the center.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Ten Galleries, Eleven Thousand Years: The Diaspora's Plan to Build India a Museum in Washington
nri-world.excerpt: After eight years of planning, organizers are launching a campaign for the India Heritage Center — what would be the first U.S. institution devoted entirely to India's civilizational story.
nri-world.image_caption: A museum gallery interior, illustrating the kind of immersive exhibition space planned for the proposed India Heritage Center
nri-world.nri_angle: A permanent national museum answers a problem the diaspora keeps solving in pieces — how to pass a civilizational inheritance to a second generation fluent in American life but distant from its roots. It also tests whether a community that gives generously to universities and temples will fund a slower, less personal kind of cultural infrastructure.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Twenty Years On, a King Still Toasts the Diaspora That Helped Him Build a Charity
nri-world.excerpt: King Charles III joined the British Asian Trust's 20th-anniversary gala in London, where the diaspora-funded charity raised over £1 million and underscored how Britain's wealthiest minority became a donor class.
nri-world.image_caption: King Charles III, Royal Founding Patron of the British Asian Trust, which marked its 20th anniversary in London
nri-world.nri_angle: The British Asian Trust inverts the old migrant narrative: instead of remitting earnings home, Britain's 1.9 million Indian-origin residents now pool wealth through a British institution to fund South Asian development — a marker of a community confident enough in its standing to give at scale.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Town of 25,000 Is About to Host 8,000 Sikhs. Squamish's Nagar Kirtan Returns After the Fire.
nri-world.excerpt: A mountain resort town north of Vancouver revives its Sikh procession on June 20, two years after a wildfire cancelled it — and turns a 17th-century martyrdom into a fixture of the civic calendar.
nri-world.image_caption: A Nagar Kirtan procession winds through the streets, devotees following the float carrying the Guru Granth Sahib
nri-world.nri_angle: For Sikhs in British Columbia, carrying the faith out of the gurdwara and onto a small town's main street is how a visible minority converts private devotion into public belonging — and the langar does the explaining a sermon cannot.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Four Million Jains, Eight Hundred Teenagers, One New Jersey Ballroom: How a Tiny Faith Refuses to Thin Out
nri-world.excerpt: The 17th Young Jains of America convention, July 2-5, is one of the largest gatherings of Jain youth outside India — and a case study in how a small diaspora fights the third-generation problem.
nri-world.image_caption: An ornately carved Jain temple, the kind of architectural tradition the diaspora works to keep meaningful for youth raised abroad
nri-world.nri_angle: Too small to rely on ambient culture or dense temple networks, Jains in North America have to organize their faith's survival deliberately — making the YJA convention a sharp, instructive version of the transmission problem every diaspora family faces.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Banks Want to Lend You the Dollars to Deposit With Them — and GIFT City Is the Catch
markets-finance.excerpt: Lenders are pressing the RBI to let their GIFT City branches finance the diaspora dollar-deposit scheme designed to shore up the rupee. Nomura reckons the plan could pull in $55 billion — most of it from NRIs — with the bulk arriving by September.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian and US currency; banks want to fund the RBI's diaspora dollar-deposit scheme via GIFT City branches
markets-finance.nri_angle: This entire scheme is built around the diaspora's dollars — it is NRIs the RBI is trying to coax into Indian banks to defend the rupee — so the mechanics of how banks fund it, and the leverage being negotiated behind the scenes, directly shape the returns and risks facing any overseas Indian weighing an FCNR deposit this summer.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Indians Pulled Back From the Stock Market in May — but Their Monthly SIPs Hit a Record Anyway
markets-finance.excerpt: Equity mutual fund inflows fell 40 percent to a 12-month low as global jitters spooked lump-sum investors, yet automated SIP contributions climbed to an all-time high of ₹26,688 crore — a sign of how deeply disciplined investing has taken root.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee notes; monthly SIP contributions hit a record even as equity fund inflows slumped in May
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs who invest in Indian mutual funds through SIPs to stay financially anchored to home, the data is reassuring: India's market is now propped up by steady domestic discipline rather than fickle foreign money, meaning the rupee-cost-averaging strategy many diaspora investors quietly run every month is exactly the behaviour holding the market up.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Five-Day Market Rally Just Snapped — and It Was the IT Giants That Broke It.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Sensex and Nifty slid on Friday as the Nifty IT index crashed to a three-year low, dragged down by an Accenture warning that has put Infosys, Wipro and TCS squarely in investors' crosshairs.
markets-finance.image_caption: An Indian stock-market display; the Sensex and Nifty fell as IT stocks slid to a three-year low
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's most personal trade — many NRIs work for or hold shares in Infosys, TCS, Wipro and Accenture itself, and a three-year low in the IT index driven by cautious US client spending speaks directly to both their portfolios and their job security in the tech corridors of New Jersey, Texas and the Bay Area.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Cheaper Oil Should Be Lifting the Rupee. India's Own Central Bank Is Quietly Holding It Back.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India's short-dollar forward book has ballooned to a record near $110 billion, and unwinding it — along with hedging the dollars Indian banks are now borrowing abroad — is set to cap the rupee's recovery even as oil sits at three-month lows. For NRIs, it explains why the currency has steadied near 94.5 rather than surged.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee currency; the RBI's record forward book is set to cap the rupee's recovery despite cheaper oil
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs watching the rupee to time remittances, deposits and Indian investments need to understand why a clear tailwind — cheap oil — is not translating into a stronger currency: the RBI's record forward-book overhang means dollar inflows are being absorbed to rebuild reserves rather than allowed to lift the rupee.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Banks Are Rushing to Borrow Dollars Abroad — and the RBI Just Made It Cheaper to Do So
markets-finance.excerpt: HDFC Bank, State Bank of India and Bank of Baroda are all tapping the overseas dollar-bond market this month, the first to use a new Reserve Bank facility that subsidises the cost of hedging foreign borrowing. Bankers expect $15–20 billion to flow in over the next six months — a deliberate effort to defend the rupee and pull in foreign capital.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian rupee currency; India's banks are raising dollars overseas under a new RBI subsidised hedging window
markets-finance.nri_angle: NRIs hold a direct stake in the rupee's stability — through remittances, NRE/FCNR deposits and Indian bank shares — and this coordinated push to draw dollars into the banking system is one of the clearest signs of how hard New Delhi is working to steady the currency and fund the economy's growth.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The World's Biggest Investors Are Pouring Billions Into India's Data Centres — the Quiet Backbone of the AI Boom
markets-finance.excerpt: Canada's national pension fund just committed $740 million to an Indian data-centre operator, Apple supplier Jabil teamed up with Adani to build AI hardware in the country, and more than $50 billion of digital-infrastructure spending is now in the pipeline. As global capital races to build the physical plumbing of artificial intelligence, India is emerging as a favoured destination — and a fresh theme for NRI investors.
markets-finance.image_caption: Inside a data centre; global investors are pouring billions into India's data-centre capacity to power the AI boom
markets-finance.nri_angle: Many NRIs work in the very technology and finance industries driving the global AI build-out, and want exposure to India's growth story beyond real estate and fixed deposits; the data-centre boom — backed by the world's largest pension funds and conglomerates — is becoming one of the most investable expressions of that story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Cleared the Way for Banks to Pay NRIs More on Their Deposits — But Only Until September.
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has temporarily scrapped the interest-rate ceilings on fresh FCNR(B) and longer-tenure NRE deposits through September 30, freeing banks to compete for overseas money as New Delhi scrambles to defend a battered rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian currency; the RBI has lifted rate caps on select NRI deposits until September 30 to attract overseas funds
markets-finance.nri_angle: This is one of the most directly actionable moves for NRIs all year: with rate caps lifted on FCNR(B) and long NRE deposits until September 30, banks are about to compete for diaspora dollars — meaning the rates Indians abroad earn on parked savings could jump, but only inside a closing window.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Made It Easier for NRIs to Buy Indian Stocks — RBI Opens a New Repatriable Rupee Account
markets-finance.excerpt: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to let individuals living abroad open dedicated repatriable rupee accounts for investing in listed Indian shares, with sale proceeds free to be sent back overseas. A new 'Individual Foreign Investor' category streamlines the long-tangled plumbing of cross-border equity investment.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has amended its foreign-exchange rules to ease how individuals abroad invest in listed Indian shares
markets-finance.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs want a stake in India's growth story but have long been deterred by a maze of account types, custodial rules and repatriation friction; this RBI amendment is aimed squarely at them, simplifying how a person abroad can buy Indian shares and — just as importantly — get their money back out.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold's Record Run Has Stalled. After a Blistering Two-Year Rally, the Fed Just Took the Wind Out of It.
markets-finance.excerpt: Bullion that surged 64% in 2025 — its best year in nearly five decades — has slid back below $4,400 an ounce, sinking to a seven-month low this month as a US-Iran peace deal, falling oil and a Federal Reserve hinting at rate hikes drain the fear that powered the climb. In India, prices have eased even as a steep new import duty bites.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold bullion bars; bullion's record rally has stalled as the Federal Reserve hints at rate hikes
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is not merely an asset for the Indian diaspora but a cultural reflex — the default store of value, the wedding gift, the hedge sent home — and after years of one-way gains, the metal's sudden wobble forces NRIs to reckon with whether they are buying a safe haven or chasing a peak that has already passed.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Largest Stock Exchange Is Finally Going Public. After a Decade of Delays, the NSE Just Filed Its IPO Papers.
markets-finance.excerpt: The National Stock Exchange — the world's busiest derivatives platform — has filed draft papers for a pure offer-for-sale of up to 149 million shares worth roughly $3 billion, ending a listing saga that began in 2016 and handing long-waiting investors a multi-billion-dollar windfall.
markets-finance.image_caption: A stock exchange trading environment; India's NSE has filed draft papers for its long-delayed IPO
markets-finance.nri_angle: The NSE is the exchange where most of India's listed wealth changes hands — the very market NRIs tap through index funds, ETFs and direct holdings — and owning a slice of the bourse itself, alongside a record year of Indian mega-listings, gives the diaspora a rare chance to bet on the plumbing of India's markets rather than any single stock.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An India-US Trade Deal Is Suddenly Close. The US Trade Chief Visits This Month to Seal the First Tranche.
markets-finance.excerpt: US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer travels to New Delhi on June 23-24 to put final touches on an interim agreement, with India's commerce minister signaling the first tranche could be done by mid-July. With a US-Iran truce cooling oil and the World Bank lifting its growth forecast, the macro backdrop has rarely looked better.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who said the first tranche of an India-US trade deal could be concluded by mid-July
markets-finance.nri_angle: An India-US trade pact sits at the center of the diaspora's two worlds — it shapes the export sectors and equities many NRIs invest in, the rupee that governs how far their remittances stretch, and the broader US-India relationship that frames diaspora life in America.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India's Defence Production Hits a Record ₹1.78 Lakh Crore — and the Stocks Riding the Boom Just Surged
markets-finance.excerpt: Government data shows India's annual defence output jumped 15.6 percent to an all-time high, with exports leaping 62 percent to nearly ₹38,500 crore and the private sector's share at a record. The Nifty India Defence index rose 3.9 percent as investors bet the 'Make in India' arms push has real momentum.
markets-finance.image_caption: India's defence production hit a record in FY26; the Nifty India Defence index surged 3.9 percent as exports jumped 62 percent
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's defence-manufacturing boom has become one of the most-watched investment themes for NRIs seeking exposure to the country's industrial rise — a story of self-reliance and export ambition that resonates with diaspora investors looking beyond IT and banks for the next structural growth story.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Neeraj Chopra Finished Fourth on His Comeback. The Number That Matters Is 85.69.
sports.excerpt: After 275 days out with a back injury, India's two-time Olympic medallist returned in Doha well short of his best — but his season's-best throw cleared the Commonwealth Games qualifying mark, and that was the point all along.
sports.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra, who returned from a back injury to finish fourth at the 2026 Doha Diamond League
sports.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is the rare Indian track-and-field superstar the diaspora has made appointment viewing, and his healthy return from a long injury lay-off — with a Commonwealth Games berth already secured — keeps alive the medal hopes NRIs rally behind at every global championship.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: An Ankle Twisted in the Powerplay Ended One World Cup. It Began Another for an Uncapped Spinner Who Was Already in England.
sports.excerpt: Shreyanka Patil is out of the Women's T20 World Cup after injuring her ankle against the Netherlands. Her replacement, 24-year-old legspinner Prema Rawat, has never played for India — and got the call while on an India A tour bus in England.
sports.image_caption: India's women's cricket team with the 2025 Women's Cricket World Cup trophy
sports.nri_angle: India's women's cricket team became a unifying obsession for NRIs after the 2025 50-over World Cup title, and the squad's depth — an uncapped spinner stepping in for an injured star without missing a beat — is exactly the kind of story the diaspora rallies behind as the team chases its first T20 World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Was Born in Paris, His Mother Is Congolese, and His Tamil Roots Run Through a Caribbean Island. Meet the Fourth Indian at This World Cup.
sports.excerpt: Samuel Moutoussamy played all 90 minutes of DR Congo's 1-1 draw with Portugal in Houston — the least-known of the four players carrying Indian heritage onto the 2026 World Cup stage, and the one with the longest, strangest journey home to it.
sports.image_caption: DR Congo midfielder Samuel Moutoussamy, of Tamil-Guadeloupean and Congolese descent, one of four players of Indian origin at the 2026 World Cup
sports.nri_angle: Samuel Moutoussamy is the fourth and least-known player of Indian descent at the 2026 World Cup — and the one with the deepest diaspora thread, tracing his Tamil roots to 19th-century indentured migrants in the French Caribbean island of Guadeloupe. For a diaspora that has never seen India reach a World Cup, he is an unlikely point of connection, and his June 27 group game against Uzbekistan in Atlanta will be within reach of America's South Asian community.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Two From Two, and the One Trophy They've Never Won Looks Closer Than Ever
sports.excerpt: India's women, reigning 50-over world champions, have opened the T20 World Cup in England with a 64-run rout of Pakistan and a record-breaking 95-run demolition of the Netherlands — and a diaspora that has waited a generation for this is watching.
sports.image_caption: India vice-captain Smriti Mandhana, whose back-to-back player-of-the-match displays have anchored India's unbeaten start to the 2026 Women's T20 World Cup
sports.nri_angle: India's women, reigning 50-over world champions, are chasing the one global title that has always eluded them — and a diaspora across England, the US and Canada is watching, in stadiums in Birmingham, Leeds and Manchester or on JioHotstar streams at all hours. After last year's home-soil ODI breakthrough, an unbeaten T20 World Cup start has given a generation of NRI fans permission to dream of a first T20 crown.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: He Is the Son of an Anglo-Indian Mother and a Tamil Father. On Friday, He Could Play the World Cup Hosts in Seattle.
sports.excerpt: Melbourne-born Nishan Velupillay is the least-talked-about of the World Cup's players of Indian heritage — a Socceroos forward who came off the bench in Australia's opening win and now waits in the wings against the United States.
sports.image_caption: Nishan Velupillay training for Melbourne Victory; the Anglo-Indian, Sri Lankan-Tamil forward is in Australia's 2026 World Cup squad
sports.nri_angle: Velupillay is part of the first World Cup to feature multiple players of Indian heritage at once — and for the large South Asian communities of America's West Coast, watching a Melbourne-born son of an Anglo-Indian mother and Tamil father potentially face the host USA in Seattle is a bittersweet point of pride in a sport India has never reached.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Nine Games, Zero Wins — Then They Beat the World Champions. India's Hockey Team Just Ended Its Misery in Rotterdam.
sports.excerpt: Two days after their worst Pro League campaign hit rock bottom, India dismantled reigning world champions Germany 3-1 — on the same night Manpreet Singh became the most-capped player in Indian hockey history.
sports.image_caption: Manpreet Singh, who became the most-capped player in Indian hockey history during India's 3-1 win over Germany
sports.nri_angle: Hockey is India's most decorated Olympic sport — eight golds and the deepest national sporting memory — and this win over the reigning world champions, on the night captain-class veteran Manpreet Singh became India's most-capped player ever, is the kind of redemption story that resonates with NRIs who inherited that history from grandparents who watched India dominate the game.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: America's Cricket Season Opened With Its Highest-Ever Chase. A 41-Year-Old From Pretoria Made 113 to Win It.
sports.excerpt: Faf du Plessis, captain of the Chennai-owned Texas Super Kings, hauled down a mountainous 221 in 18.3 overs to launch Major League Cricket's fourth season in Grand Prairie — the Dallas suburb that has become the capital of cricket in America.
sports.image_caption: Faf du Plessis, captain of the Texas Super Kings, whose unbeaten 113 sealed a record chase on the opening night of Major League Cricket 2026
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket is the most tangible expression of cricket's American chapter — a professional league built in the US suburbs the Indian and South Asian diaspora calls home, with Grand Prairie near Dallas as its capital. The Texas Super Kings are co-owned by the IPL's Chennai Super Kings, and the record opening-night chase gives NRIs in the US a top-tier league in their own time zone, their own city, and a professional pathway for the next generation that did not exist a decade ago.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: The Injury He Hid, the Coach He Left: Neeraj Chopra Returns to the Runway in Doha
sports.excerpt: After nine months away — his longest absence since Olympic gold — India's greatest track-and-field star opens his 2026 season on Friday with a startling admission about Tokyo, and a quiet rebellion against the foreign-expert model: he has gone back to an Indian coach.
sports.image_caption: Neeraj Chopra, India's double Olympic medallist, returns to competition at the Doha Diamond League after a nine-month injury layoff
sports.nri_angle: Neeraj Chopra is the Indian diaspora's rarest icon — an individual-sport world conqueror with no cricketing safety net — and NRIs across the US, UK and Canada set alarms to watch him compete. His return at the Doha Diamond League after a nine-month injury layoff carries an extra charge: he has left the legendary Czech coach Jan Zelezny to train under an Indian mentor, Jaiveer 'Jay' Chaudhary, a quiet rejection of the foreign-expert premium the diaspora knows so well, and a bet on his own instincts ahead of the Commonwealth and Asian Games.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Is 18, She Beat the World No. 10 in Washington, and She Is India's Best Shot at an Olympic Squash Medal
sports.excerpt: Anahat Singh has cracked the world's top 20, defended her Indian Open title in Mumbai and become the youngest Asian woman ever to climb that high. With squash entering the Olympics for the first time at LA 2028, the teenager from Delhi is carrying a sport — and a diaspora — on her shoulders.
sports.image_caption: Indian squash great Joshna Chinappa, pictured after a junior title win — part of the generation that paved the way for teenage No. 1 Anahat Singh
sports.nri_angle: Squash is quietly one of the diaspora's sports — South Asian families fill racquet clubs in New Jersey, suburban London and the Greater Toronto Area — yet the community rarely sees itself represented at the elite level. Anahat Singh, 18, of Delhi, has cracked the world's top 20 (the youngest Asian woman ever to do so), beaten the world No. 10, and become India's best hope for a medal when squash debuts at the LA 2028 Olympics. A composed, fearless role model for NRI families and their daughters.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Is 21, She Is From Hyderabad, and She Just Broke a World Record on the Germans' Home Range
sports.excerpt: At the ISSF World Cup in Munich, Esha Singh shot 43 out of 50 to win the women's 25m pistol gold — a score that now stands as both the senior and junior world record. She beat the reigning Olympic champion and a former world champion to do it. India's quiet shooting empire just got a new face.
sports.image_caption: Indian pistol shooter Esha Singh, who set senior and junior 25m pistol world records (43/50) to win gold at the 2026 ISSF World Cup in Munich
sports.nri_angle: Shooting rarely makes the diaspora highlight reels that cricket and chess command, yet it has quietly become one of India's most reliable medal factories — a discipline where Indian women routinely beat established European and East Asian powers on their home ranges. Esha Singh, 21, from Hyderabad, outshot the reigning Olympic champion and a former world champion in Munich to set senior and junior world records, a quieter, more precise kind of pride for NRIs to follow.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: She Coached at MIT, Then the Grizzlies. Now Sonia Raman Is the First Indian-Origin Head Coach in the WNBA — and the Hardest Part Has Only Just Begun.
sports.excerpt: A walk-on guard who became a lawyer, then the winningest coach in MIT history, then the first Indian-American woman on an NBA bench, Raman took over the Seattle Storm this season. At 3-12, the rebuild is brutal — but the barrier she broke is permanent.
sports.image_caption: Seattle Storm guard Flau'jae Johnson during the 2026 WNBA season, Sonia Raman's first as head coach
sports.nri_angle: Sonia Raman is the first person of Indian origin to be a head coach in the WNBA — and earlier was the first Indian-American woman to coach in the NBA — a barrier-breaking career that offers South Asian families in America a powerful counter-example to the idea that professional sport is not a serious path.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: A Son of Kerala Is About to Make World Cup History — in Qatar's Colours
sports.excerpt: Tahsin Mohammed Jamshid, the Doha-born winger with roots in Kannur, stands on the brink of becoming the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup.
sports.image_caption: The Qatar national football team, which 20-year-old Kerala-origin winger Tahsin Jamshid represents at the 2026 World Cup
sports.nri_angle: For decades, football-obsessed Kerala has poured its passion into supporting Brazil, Argentina and Germany at the World Cup without ever having a player of its own on the stage. Tahsin Jamshid — born in Doha to Malayali parents from Kannur — is poised to become the first footballer of Indian origin to play at a FIFA World Cup, a landmark for the Gulf's vast Malayali expatriate community and a bittersweet milestone for an India whose own men's team has never qualified.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Google Put Gemini in a $99 Speaker. The Real Target Is the Phone in Every Indian Pocket.
technology.excerpt: Sundar Pichai is smuggling his AI into the devices people already own — and India is the test bed, not the afterthought.
technology.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, who is steering the company's Gemini-everywhere strategy.
technology.nri_angle: Indian Americans sit on both sides of this launch — as the engineers inside Alphabet whose teams live or die by Gemini, and as NRIs whose families in India are Google's first test market for its AI-everywhere strategy.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Nvidia's Biggest Threat Isn't a Rival. It's the Customers Now Selling Their Own Chips.
technology.excerpt: Amazon and Google are pushing custom AI silicon into the open market — and Indian engineers are building hardware on every side of the fight.
technology.image_caption: Close-up of microchips on a circuit board, the contested hardware at the center of the AI chip war.
technology.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers staff the silicon, memory, networking, and security layers of the AI stack at once, so the breakup of Nvidia's monopoly directly shapes diaspora careers and NRI investment portfolios.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Satya Nadella Warned Against AI Monopolies. Days Later He Started Charging by the Task.
technology.excerpt: Microsoft's new usage-based Copilot agents reveal where the most valuable work is heading — and what it means for the Indians who do so much of it.
technology.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, who is reshaping Copilot around autonomous, usage-billed AI agents.
technology.nri_angle: Microsoft's pivot to billing for autonomous AI work hits the structured, multi-step knowledge tasks that Indian engineers and IT-services firms built their economic model on, redrawing which careers survive.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Accenture's Stock Just Cratered to a 7-Year Low. The Company That Employs the Most Indians Is Flashing a Warning.
technology.excerpt: Bookings shrank, AI clients are stalling at the pilot stage, and the firm has stopped breaking out its AI revenue. For Indian engineers, the world's biggest consultancy is the canary in the coal mine.
technology.image_caption: Accenture chair and CEO Julie Sweet speaking at the World Economic Forum
technology.nri_angle: Accenture employs more Indians than any other firm on earth; its stalling bookings and AI-driven caution are an early signal for the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers whose careers run through global IT services.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: An American Manufacturer Is Teaming With Adani to Build India's AI Backbone. The Diaspora Should Watch Where the Racks Get Made.
technology.excerpt: Jabil and the Adani Group plan a vertically integrated factory for AI data-center hardware in India — racks, cooling, power — chasing a market they peg at over $3 trillion. It is the unglamorous half of the AI boom, and India wants it.
technology.image_caption: Server racks lit blue inside a modern data center
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing whether India can move up the AI value chain beyond software services, a US-India factory making the physical hardware of data centers is the most concrete test yet of the 'build it at home' thesis.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: DeepSeek Just Raised $7.4 Billion to Stay Chinese. India's AI Startups Are Watching the Playbook Closely.
technology.excerpt: The lab that rattled Silicon Valley took outside money for the first time — through a structure designed so its founder never loses control. For India's sovereign-AI push and the diaspora that funds it, it is a lesson in how to scale without selling out.
technology.image_caption: A modern server unit in a blue-lit data center, representing AI compute infrastructure
technology.nri_angle: DeepSeek's founder-control funding model is a template India's own AI champions — and the NRI investors backing them — are studying as they try to build sovereign AI without ceding control to foreign capital.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: The Men Who Run Microsoft and Google Just Bought a Piece of Lord's. The Buyer's List Reads Like an NRI Yearbook.
technology.excerpt: A consortium led by Palo Alto Networks' Nikesh Arora — with Satya Nadella, Sundar Pichai and Shantanu Narayen — paid roughly £195 million for 49% of London Spirit, outbidding an IPL billionaire.
technology.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora, who led the consortium that bought a 49% stake in London Spirit.
technology.nri_angle: Four of the most powerful Indian-origin executives in global tech just turned their personal wealth toward cricket at Lord's — a vivid sign of where diaspora capital and cultural identity are converging.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Adobe Is Giving Its AI Away for Free. Shantanu Narayen Is Betting the Crowd Comes Back to Pay.
technology.excerpt: On its Q2 call, Adobe paused Creative Cloud price hikes and pushed free versions of its AI tools — freemium users jumped to 90 million — and raised full-year guidance even as the strategy squeezes near-term revenue.
technology.image_caption: Adobe chairman and CEO Shantanu Narayen, who is steering the company through its AI transition.
technology.nri_angle: Adobe under Indian-origin CEO Shantanu Narayen is a core holding for many NRI investors and a major employer of Indian engineers — its bet to give AI away and chase scale over margin is a wager the whole diaspora-heavy software sector is now making.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Razorpay Just Filed Quietly for Its IPO. India's Payment Giants Are Lining Up to Cash Out — and NRIs Want In.
technology.excerpt: The Bengaluru fintech confidentially submitted its draft prospectus to SEBI as UPI volumes hit record highs, joining a 2026 pipeline that already includes the NSE and a wave of consumer-tech listings.
technology.image_caption: The Razorpay logo; the payments giant has filed confidentially for an IPO as India's fintech leaders line up to go public
technology.nri_angle: A generation of Indian fintech unicorns NRIs read about for years is finally heading to public markets — turning private bets into something diaspora investors can actually own, if they understand the cross-border rules.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: An Indian IT Giant Just Bought Into the AI That Could Replace It. The Logic Is Colder Than It Looks.
technology.excerpt: HCLTech's $150 million bet on Sarvam AI is the first time an Indian services firm has taken a real stake in a homegrown model-maker. It is less a vote of confidence than a hedge.
technology.image_caption: HCLTech chief executive C Vijayakumar, who is steering the company into sovereign AI.
technology.nri_angle: For the hundreds of thousands of Indians whose careers run through TCS, Infosys, Wipro and HCL — on H-1Bs in New Jersey or in Bengaluru delivery centers — this deal signals which skills the services industry will pay for next, and which it is quietly writing off.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Threads Just Hit 500 Million Users. The Quiet Engine Behind It Is India.
technology.excerpt: Meta's three-year-old text app is now the size of X — and much of its organic, sticky growth is coming from the creators, fandoms and diaspora arguments that flourish in the Indian internet.
technology.image_caption: The Threads logo; Meta's text-based app crossed 500 million monthly users, with India among its fastest-growing markets
technology.nri_angle: Threads has become the default room where Indian creators, cricket fandoms and NRI commentators argue in real time — so where Meta steers the app next directly shapes how the diaspora talks to itself, and how brands reach it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Ghar Wapsi: India's Startups Are Sprinting Home Before They IPO. NRI Investors Should Read the Fine Print.
technology.excerpt: Meesho, Zepto, Pine Labs and now Pocket FM are unwinding their offshore holding companies to list in Mumbai. The 'reverse flip' is reshaping who gets to own India's next public tech.
technology.nri_angle: When a startup moves its parent from Delaware or Singapore back to India ahead of an IPO, the listing happens on Indian exchanges — changing exactly how, and whether, an NRI in the US can buy in, and what tax bill comes with it.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Salman Khan Wants a Turquoise Bracelet Banned From the Movies. The Delhi High Court Just Told Him to Wait.
entertainment.excerpt: A low-budget film called 'Kala Hiran' has India's biggest star in court, the director firing back with 'Salman isn't God', and a producer claiming death threats from a Pakistani terrorist. The hearing now stretches to July 1.
entertainment.image_caption: Salman Khan, who has taken the makers of Kala Hiran to the Delhi High Court (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Jim Sarbh Shaved His Head for Real and Made a Show Without a Single Curse Word. India Might Send It to the Emmys.
entertainment.excerpt: 'Made In India: A Titan Story' is the quiet word-of-mouth hit of the summer — a corporate drama about a wristwatch that families are watching together without skipping a frame. Now its producer says a second Emmy nomination for Sarbh is firmly on the table.
entertainment.image_caption: Jim Sarbh, who plays Titan visionary Xerxes Desai in Made In India: A Titan Story (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.excerpt: The streamers stacked everything onto one Friday. From Drishyam 3 to Sonali Bendre’s comeback — here are the eight picks worth your subscription, and exactly where to find them.

entertainment.title: Allu Arjun Is Summoned to Court Over the Pushpa 2 Stampede. The Man Who Plays the Untouchable Hero Must Now Stand Before a Judge.
entertainment.excerpt: Eighteen months after a fan died in the crush at a Pushpa 2 premiere, Hyderabad's Nampally Court has ordered the superstar to appear in person on June 22.

entertainment.title: The 1920 Franchise Is Back to Haunt You. Vikram Bhatt and Anand Pandit Reunite for 1920: Cold Winter.
entertainment.excerpt: India's most durable horror brand returns for another candlelit haunting — the eighth chapter in a saga that has been scaring the diaspora for eighteen years.

entertainment.title: Los Angeles Just Gave Diljit Dosanjh His Own Day. The Boy From Dosanjh Kalan Now Owns a Date on the City Calendar.
entertainment.excerpt: The LA City Council has declared January 6, 2027 'Diljit Dosanjh Day' — a civic honour for the man who turned Punjabi into a stadium language. He found out the same week he sold out Crypto.com Arena.

entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Nora Fatehi Walked Onto a World Cup Stage in Toronto and Became the Most Googled Bollywood Star on Earth
entertainment.excerpt: In a red ensemble, flanked by hundreds of dancers, she performed the official FIFA anthem 'Siir Siir' before Canada's match — and outpaced Priyanka, Deepika and Alia in global searches overnight. Twice now, the World Cup has belonged to her.
entertainment.image_caption: Nora Fatehi, who headlined the FIFA World Cup 2026 opening ceremony in Toronto (Wikimedia Commons)

entertainment.title: Cocktail 2 Opens Big. Fourteen Years On, the Diaspora's Favourite Love Triangle Is Pouring Again.
entertainment.excerpt: Shahid, Kriti and Rashmika's spiritual successor lands a four-star verdict, 100K+ advance tickets and an 8.83 cr start — proving there's still an audience for a love story with no superheroes attached.
entertainment.image_caption: Official poster for Cocktail 2, starring Shahid Kapoor, Kriti Sanon and Rashmika Mandanna

entertainment.title: Dhurandhar 2 Lands on Netflix India Today. The Most-Watched Indian Film in History Just Got Another Stage.
entertainment.excerpt: Ranveer Singh's 1,800-crore revenge epic crossed 70 million digital views, lapped RRR, and is now streaming on Netflix India — while the diaspora has had the uncut 'Raw & Undekha' version for over a month.
entertainment.image_caption: Official poster for Dhurandhar: The Revenge, starring Ranveer Singh
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Rajkumar Hirani Is Finally Doing OTT — and He's Bringing His Son and Circuit Along for the Ride
entertainment.excerpt: After Munna Bhai, 3 Idiots, PK and Dunki, the man who makes India cry-laugh is making his streaming debut with 'Pritam and Pedro.' Arshad Warsi is back. So is a kid named Vir Hirani. July 3, JioHotstar.

entertainment.title: Rajkummar Rao Gained 10 Kilos to Become the Man Who Sent Kasab to the Gallows. The Prahaar Teaser Is a Gut-Punch.
entertainment.excerpt: Attached to Cocktail 2's prints and dropped online Friday, the first look at 'Prahaar – The Ujjwal Nikam Story' trades horror-comedy charm for a courtroom that still smells of cordite. Stree's golden boy has never looked heavier, or hungrier.
entertainment.image_caption: Rajkummar Rao, who plays prosecutor Ujjwal Nikam in Prahaar (Wikimedia Commons)

lifestyle-health.title: The Smartwatch on Your Wrist May Be Quietly Doing Your Heart a Favour, a Review of 14 Trials Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Pooling 14 clinical trials, researchers found that heart-disease patients who used fitness apps or wearables walked nearly 1,100 more steps a day than those who did not — a small, low-cost nudge with outsized relevance for a community that develops heart disease early.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A fitness tracker; a review of 14 trials found heart patients using such tools walked about 1,100 more steps daily
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: People of Indian origin suffer heart attacks up to a decade earlier than other populations and are among the most enthusiastic adopters of smartwatches and fitness rings — so the finding that a device many NRIs already wear can measurably push them to move more turns a gadget on the wrist into a genuine, low-cost cardiac-prevention tool for the diaspora.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Head Injury Can Raise the Risk of Brain Disease. New Research Says the Danger May Run Both Ways.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of more than 55,000 older veterans finds that those recently diagnosed with stroke, dementia, epilepsy or Parkinson's were far more likely to have suffered a traumatic brain injury — a finding that reframes fall prevention as brain protection for ageing parents.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult walking with support; falls are the main cause of traumatic brain injury in the elderly
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs are caring for ageing parents — some living abroad with them, many supporting elders back in India from a distance — and this research delivers a sharp, actionable warning: a parent newly diagnosed with dementia, stroke, epilepsy or Parkinson's is in a high-risk window for a fall-related head injury, making home fall-proofing one of the most concrete things a diaspora family can do.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Carrying Extra Weight Now Linked to 19 Cancers, Not 13 — and South Asians Show Up in the Fine Print
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Pooling more than 1.5 million cancer cases across 23 countries, a sweeping new review widens the list of weight-related cancers and finds the risks differ sharply by sex and region — with striking gaps in data on South Asian populations.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A waist measurement; a review of 1.5 million cancer cases links higher BMI to 19 cancer types
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: South Asians develop diabetes and heart disease at lower body weights than Western populations, yet this very review flags that South Asia is badly under-represented in long-term cancer data — meaning diaspora families are being handed risk numbers built largely on European and East Asian bodies, and should treat even a modest waistline as a cancer-prevention issue, not just a cosmetic one.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Weight-Loss Drugs May Do Something Unexpected for Men: Lift Testosterone and Improve Sperm
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Early data presented at a major endocrinology meeting suggests GLP-1 medicines like Ozempic may raise testosterone and improve sperm quality in men with obesity — a tentative finding in a field where male fertility is rarely discussed openly.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A GLP-1 injection pen; early data suggests the weight-loss drugs may improve testosterone and sperm quality in men
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Male infertility is one of the most stigmatised and silently borne health issues in Indian families, where the burden of childlessness is too often placed on women; framing it as a treatable, hormonally-influenced medical condition — one that weight and metabolic health can move — gives diaspora couples a less shame-laden, more clinical way to seek help.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Harvard Just Found the Strength-Training Sweet Spot for a Longer Life. It Is Less Than You Think.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Following 150,000 adults for more than three decades, researchers report that about 90 to 120 minutes of strength training a week is tied to the biggest drop in the risk of early death — and that piling on far more brings little extra benefit.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Strength training with weights; a 30-year study of 150,000 adults found 90-120 minutes a week is the longevity sweet spot
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Strength training is the great blind spot in many Indian-origin households — elders walk for cardio but rarely lift, even as South Asians carry more body fat and less muscle for their size, raising diabetes and heart risk; a finding that just 15-20 minutes of resistance work a day moves the longevity needle makes the habit feel achievable rather than gym-bro intimidating.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Pill May Be Quietly Driving Food Cravings, a Study of Young Women Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking 422 women over two menstrual cycles, researchers found binge-eating episodes rose on the days they took active birth control pills — a hormonal link that held even after accounting for mood and other medications.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Combined oral contraceptive pills; a study links active-pill days to more binge-eating episodes in young women
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Disordered eating is heavily stigmatised and rarely discussed in Indian families, and the contraceptive pill is increasingly used by young diaspora women — so framing sudden food cravings as a possible hormonal side effect, not a failure of willpower, gives mothers and daughters a less shame-laden way to talk about both binge eating and birth control.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Weight-Loss Drugs Were Supposed to Get People Moving. A New Study Found They Quietly Sit Down More.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Tracking 753 adults on Ozempic-style medications with fitness monitors, researchers found their daily steps and exercise minutes fell after starting the drugs — not rose. Because these medications strip away muscle along with fat, the slump is exactly the wrong response, and it carries a sharp warning for the growing number of diaspora families now reaching for them.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An injection pen; a study of 753 GLP-1 users found their daily steps and exercise fell after starting the drugs
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs like Ozempic and Wegovy are spreading fast through Indian-American and broader diaspora households already at elevated risk of muscle-poor, fat-heavy bodies and early diabetes; this study warns that the very people most drawn to the injections may be undercutting them by moving less, and losing the muscle they can least afford to lose.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Eating Your Five-a-Day May Not Be Enough. A 30,000-Person Study Says It Is the Right Plants That Protect the Heart.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: An international study measuring actual blood markers in more than 30,000 people in Britain and America found that fewer than one in five get enough flavanols — the plant compounds tied to lower cardiovascular risk — even among many who hit their fruit-and-vegetable targets. For the diaspora, the fix lies in foods already close at hand: tea, apples, berries and dark chocolate.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Fruits rich in flavanols; a 30,000-person study found most people fall short of the plant compounds tied to heart health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora families are told endlessly to eat more fruit and vegetables, but this research shows the protective payoff depends on which plants — and the richest everyday sources of heart-friendly flavanols, led by tea, are already staples in South Asian homes if chosen with intent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Cheapest Protein in the Indian Kitchen May Be the Most Protective. New Research Keeps Pointing to the Humble Dal.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A run of nutrition research keeps landing on the same unglamorous conclusion: legumes — the lentils, chickpeas and beans at the heart of Indian cooking — lower blood pressure, protect the heart and, in one landmark study of older adults, were the single most protective food group for survival. For a diaspora drifting toward Western convenience food, it is a reminder that the answer was on the thali all along.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Lentils and legumes; research repeatedly links the cheap pantry staple to lower blood pressure and longer survival
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Lentils, chickpeas and beans are the protein backbone of Indian vegetarian cooking, yet many diaspora families quietly eat less dal as schedules tighten and Western convenience food creeps in; the science says the cheapest item in their pantry is also one of the most protective against the heart disease and diabetes that strike South Asians early.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Study of 5,700 Teenagers Found What Wrecks Their Sleep — and Girls Are Paying the Steeper Price
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a survey of 5,713 adolescents published in PLOS One, a third had poor sleep quality, and the biggest culprits were a familiar trio: mental health, body weight and screen time. Girls fared markedly worse than boys. For diaspora parents fighting the nightly battle over phones, the findings put hard numbers on an instinct they already had.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A teenager on a phone at night; a study of 5,713 adolescents tied poor sleep to screen time, body weight and mental health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Diaspora parents wage a near-universal nightly struggle over screens and sleep with teenagers caught between academic pressure and phones; this large study names the three levers — screen time, weight and mental health — that actually move adolescent sleep, and flags that daughters may be carrying a heavier burden.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A High-Dose Omega-3 Pill Was Supposed to Sharpen Aging Brains. A Two-Year Trial Found It Did Nothing.
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a rigorous randomized trial published this week in the Lancet journal eBioMedicine, two years of high-dose DHA supplements raised omega-3 levels in the blood and even the brain — yet produced no improvement in memory, cognition or the size of the brain's memory centre. For a diaspora that treats fish-oil capsules as a daily insurance policy, the finding is a pointed reality check.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Omega-3 fish-oil capsules; a two-year randomized trial found high-dose DHA failed to improve memory or cognition in at-risk older adults
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Fish-oil and omega-3 capsules are among the most popular supplements in Indian-American medicine cabinets, often taken specifically to protect aging memory; this gold-standard trial suggests that for people who are otherwise unhealthy, the pills do not deliver the brain benefit so many quietly count on.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Common Vitamin B3 Supplement Helped Older Adults With Clogged Leg Arteries Walk Farther, a New Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a six-month double-blind trial from Northwestern and the University of Florida, older adults with peripheral artery disease who took nicotinamide riboside — a form of vitamin B3 that boosts the cellular fuel NAD — walked meaningfully farther than those on a placebo, with the biggest gains among those who took their pills faithfully. Adding red-wine compound resveratrol added nothing.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Older adults walking; a vitamin B3 supplement that boosts cellular NAD modestly improved walking distance in people with peripheral artery disease
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Peripheral artery disease tracks closely with the diabetes and heart disease that strike South Asians early and hard, and supervised walking therapy is often out of reach for elders living far from medical centres or with family; an affordable daily supplement that modestly improves mobility speaks directly to that gap.
